source_name: Каталог фінтех-компаній України 2023 (MFA-hosted mirror)
why_relevant: Prior-year edition of the same catalog, hosted on a Ukrainian MFA domain (stable, non-bot-defended). Valuable for time-series: comparing 2023 vs 2025 rosters shows which fintechs exited, merged or entered — a cheap proxy for market churn and competitive dynamics.

source_name: UAFIC — Фінтех-тренди / research pages
why_relevant: Association-published trend research naming segment leaders and the sponsors/partners behind each study. Useful for reading which vendors position themselves as thought leaders, and for the partner logos attached to each research programme (IFC, SECO, GGF, USF).

source_name: Національна/Незалежна асоціація банків України (НАБУ) — Банки-учасники
why_relevant: Roster of NABU member banks — historically >95% of Ukrainian banking-system assets. The canonical demand-side actor list for anyone selling into Ukrainian banks; also the base for identifying which banks are NOT members. NABU additionally lists associate members and partners (e.g. it carries a page for the Ukrainian fintech association), which extends the pointer into non-bank vendors.

source_name: Асоціація українських банків (АУБ) — Члени АУБ / AUB members
why_relevant: Ukraine's oldest banking association (founded 1990), with 70+ member organisations spanning commercial banks, state banks and non-bank financial companies. The non-bank members are the interesting part for vendor discovery. An English mirror of the member list exists, making cross-language entity matching easier. AUB is also named as an EMA partner, confirming the association network.

source_name: Український кредитно-банківський союз (УКБС / Ukrainian Credit-Banking Union)
source_subtype: association profile (proxy for an unlocated official site)
why_relevant: Third banking association (originated as the Kyiv Banking Union in 1994, renamed 2005), reported to unite ~92 financial and credit institutions plus foreign-institution representatives. Third overlapping roster helps triangulate the full bank universe and catch institutions absent from NABU/AUB. The Wikipedia entry is recorded here as the reliable entry point because the union's own domain was not confirmed in this pass.

source_name: Асоціація "IT Ukraine" — Члени Асоціації / Members
why_relevant: 72 member IT companies plus strategic partnerships with 9 regional IT clusters. Ukrainian IT service firms are the integrators and software suppliers behind bank digital projects and are direct or partner-channel competitors for systems-integration work. English mirror available at /en/members/, easing entity matching.

source_name: Асоціація підприємств інформаційних технологій України (АПІТУ) — Члени Асоціації
why_relevant: APITU is the hardware/IT-equipment side of the Ukrainian IT industry (distributors, systems integrators, equipment suppliers) as opposed to IT Ukraine's outsourcing-services membership. This is the association most likely to contain self-service terminal, kiosk and POS hardware channel partners — the closest analogue to an ATM/hardware industry body found in this pass.

source_name: Асоціація рітейлерів України (RAU) — партнери та члени
source_subtype: retail association member/partner directory + partner news feed
why_relevant: 90+ retail member companies and 30+ B2B partner companies. Retail is the acquiring/POS demand side: RAU partner announcements name payment vendors entering the merchant channel (e.g. the FONDY partnership announcement). The partner-news subsection is effectively a feed of payments-vendor go-to-market moves.

source_name: Українська Рада Бізнесу — перелік учасників (UBC member list)
why_relevant: Umbrella body whose members are themselves associations and business unions. Useful as a meta-pointer: it enumerates the Ukrainian association landscape in one place, letting this cell discover sectoral bodies (payments, retail, IT, cash handling) that do not surface in topic-keyword search.

source_name: Асоціація ЄМА — картка організації в Опендатабот (ЄДРПОУ 30401000)
why_relevant: Registry mirror for the association's own legal entity (EDRPOU 30401000, registered 29.04.1999) giving officers, address and filing history. Confirms the association's legal identity and, via founder/officer records, links to individuals who also sit in member institutions. Same pattern applies to UAFIC (EDRPOU 42031209).

source_name: Дія Бізнес — довідник підприємця: картка Асоціації ЄМА
why_relevant: State-run business handbook entry describing EMA's role and membership scope (payment systems, banks, financial companies, payment providers, MFOs). Government-hosted, stable, unlikely to be bot-defended — a good low-risk corroboration source for association descriptions and possibly a directory of other sector bodies.

source_name: UAFIC LinkedIn & X company presences (association social channels)
why_relevant: Association social channels announce new member admissions, partnerships and event sponsors faster than the website member page updates, and LinkedIn surfaces employee/affiliation graphs. EMA maintains equivalents. Useful as a low-latency change-detection layer over the directories.

source_name: OpenWay Group — news & blog (customer announcements)
why_relevant: OpenWay (WAY4) publishes named client wins in Ukraine; a 2012 post announced a leading Ukrainian bank's WAY4-based strategy, and Oschadbank's in-house processing migration to WAY4 is documented. Vendor-side disclosure of processing platform choice, scope and dates.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf — banking case studies / success stories library
why_relevant: Largest global self-service vendor's named-customer case-study library. DN divested Russia/Ukraine assets, so historic Ukrainian references are the key artefacts; regional CEE case studies (e.g. CSOB, Bank of Kielce) also reveal comparable deployment models and Ukrainian-language ATM software support.

source_name: NCR Atleos — banking portfolio and ATM-as-a-Service pages
why_relevant: Largest global ATM deployer; site carries customer references and service-model descriptions. Ukrainian named clients were not surfaced in search, so this is a monitoring target rather than a confirmed hit — but any UA reference would be authoritative on scale and product.

source_name: Auriga S.p.A. — press releases and partner announcements
why_relevant: Auriga announced a strategic partnership with Transaction Systems explicitly covering Ukraine for its WWS omnichannel/ATM platform — direct evidence of channel route into Ukrainian banks and of multivendor software competing with hardware OEM software.

source_name: Transaction Systems (TRSYS) — regional VAR/integrator newsroom
why_relevant: Regional distributor/integrator whose stated territory includes Ukraine; it resells Auriga WWS and similar platforms. Channel partners often name end-customer banks that the OEM will not. Directly relevant as a Printec-adjacent competitor in the same territory.

source_name: CS Ltd (Kharkiv) — cases and press-centre, АБС Б2
why_relevant: Dominant local core-banking vendor (Б2 claimed in roughly every second Ukrainian bank). Publishes named implementation cases (Bank Lviv CS::BI, Bank Pivdennyi, BIS Bank Visa B2B Connect) and NBU-regulatory adaptation notes — the richest Ukrainian-language vendor case-study stream and the incumbent competitor to Temenos/Finastra in UA.

source_name: Temenos — press releases / customer wins
why_relevant: Core-banking vendor that announces named bank selections with product and deployment model. No Ukrainian announcement surfaced, but the press index is the canonical place a UA win would appear and is cheap to monitor.

source_name: Finastra — Customer Stories / success stories
why_relevant: Named-customer story library for lending, payments, trade finance and financial messaging — the product areas most likely to reach mid-size Ukrainian banks. Monitoring target; no UA story confirmed in this pass.

source_name: Tietoevry — success stories and newsroom (banking)
why_relevant: Nordic banking SaaS provider with card/payment products sold beyond the Nordics; success-story and newsroom pages name client institutions. Low prior probability of Ukrainian clients but worth low-cost monitoring for card-processing outsourcing deals.

source_name: ATM Marketplace — vendor company showcases and resources
why_relevant: Aggregates vendor-supplied case studies, white papers and press for Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Auriga, Hyosung and others in one place, often preserving material later removed from vendor sites. Best single pointer for discovering new vendor case-study assets.

source_name: FeaturedCustomers — vendor customer-reference profiles
why_relevant: Indexes hundreds of vendor customer references and testimonials per vendor (Finastra profile alone lists 419), including links back to original case studies. Useful for enumerating a vendor's disclosed client base and spotting CEE/UA names quickly.

source_name: AppsRunTheWorld — customer databases by product (e.g. NCR Atleos ATM as a Service)
why_relevant: Commercial database that enumerates named customers per enterprise software product, including geography. Fast way to test whether a vendor has disclosed Ukrainian installations without reading every case study.

source_name: TAdviser — product and vendor project registries (Way4, BPC Group)
why_relevant: Wiki-style registry of vendor products and implementation projects across the post-Soviet space; retains historical BPC/SmartVista and Way4 project records including Ukrainian offices and deployments that vendors have since de-emphasised. Useful for pre-2022 baseline; treat as unverified and cross-check.

source_name: Banker.ua — press releases from Ukrainian banks and fintech-vendor features
why_relevant: Ukrainian banking trade outlet that republishes bank and vendor press releases verbatim, including vendor-partnership stories (e.g. Mastercard–Oschadbank–VDNG payment-infrastructure partnership) and explainers on how fintech vendors build bank products. Mirrors vendor claims into the local-language record.

source_name: AWS / hyperscaler customer case studies — PrivatBank
why_relevant: Non-obvious supplier-side disclosure: the cloud provider published a named Ukrainian bank case study (PrivatBank migration under wartime conditions) with architecture and timeline detail that the bank's own releases omit. Demonstrates that hyperscaler case-study libraries belong in the vendor-reference cell alongside ATM/core vendors.

source_name: AlixPartners — PrivatBank engagement case study
why_relevant: Consultancy case study on a named Ukrainian bank. Advisory-firm case pages are a parallel supplier-side channel that names Ukrainian financial institutions and describes transformation programmes that later generate technology procurement.
